**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) — Section 15 (¶ p0080).**

**What the document says.** Section 15 is the Agreement's only assignment provision: mutual consent required for any assignment, with a single carve-out for "an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate."

**Why it fails the fallback.** Two material gaps:
1. **No successor/M&A carve-out.** The affiliate carve-out does not cover a sale of Mortgage Logic.com to a third-party acquirer, so TrueLink could block or extract value from a corporate transaction.
2. **Unqualified consent standard.** Approval is not subject to a reasonableness qualifier in either direction, so consent could be withheld arbitrarily.

**What is *not* wrong.** There is no change-of-control language anywhere in the document (search returned nothing), and the termination provisions in Sections 13–14 are not CoC-triggered. So the clause avoids walk-away territory — no Vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control.

**The redline (validated ok:true).** Rewrites Section 15 to the preferred position with a single replacement: Client may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor by merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets; TrueLink's assignments remain subject to our consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and never to a Client competitor; and a Client change of control is expressly not an assignment and confers no termination or re-pricing right. The comment offers the mutual notice-based fallback if TrueLink resists the asymmetry, since the existing clause was drafted symmetrically.
